steps.title: Filtration
steps.say: Blood arrives in the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent. Glomerular pressure of 55 millimetres of mercury, minus 15 in Bowman's capsule and 30 of plasma oncotic pressure, leaves a net 10 pushing fluid out. That makes 125 millilitres a minute, about 180 litres a day, so our parcel starts as plasma water at 300 milliosmoles per kilogram.

steps.title: Proximal tubule
steps.say: In the proximal tubule, sodium is pumped out and water follows it straight away. So the parcel loses about 65 percent of its volume, yet its osmolality stays at 300. All of the glucose and about 80 percent of the bicarbonate are taken back here too.

steps.title: Descending limb
steps.say: The thin descending limb lets water through but not salt. As it dives into an ever saltier medulla, water leaves by osmosis, so the fluid keeps pace with the interstitium around it. By the tip of the loop it is about 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram, and only about 9 percent of the filtrate is left.

steps.title: Thick ascending limb
steps.say: Now the wall flips. The thick ascending limb has no water channels, but its N-K-two-C-L cotransporter pumps salt out, so the volume stays the same while the fluid gets more and more dilute, down to about 100. That pumped salt is what builds the 300 to 1200 gradient, and it is exactly what furosemide blocks.

steps.title: Macula densa, DCT
steps.say: The limb returns to touch its own glomerulus at the macula densa, which senses the salt arriving. In the distal convoluted tubule, the thiazide-sensitive sodium chloride carrier removes a little more salt, and the wall is still water-tight, so the fluid stays dilute, at about 90.

steps.title: Aldosterone, ADH
steps.say: In the collecting duct, aldosterone makes the principal cells take up sodium and secrete potassium. With ADH present, aquaporin-2 is inserted, so water leaves toward the 300 milliosmole cortex, and the fluid climbs from about 90 back to nearly 300.

steps.title: Concentrated urine
steps.say: The duct then runs down through the same gradient the loop built. Water keeps leaving into the hypertonic medulla, so the urine ends up at over 1100 milliosmoles per kilogram, with well under 1 percent of the filtrate left. That is about 1 litre a day from 180, which is why more than 99 percent of the filtrate is reabsorbed.
